title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
subtitle: Daniel Kahneman
description: Kahneman's synthesis of decades of research (much with Amos Tversky) on two modes of thought—fast, intuitive System 1 and slow, deliberate System 2—and the systematic biases that arise when the fast system is left unchecked.

title: Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion
subtitle: Robert Cialdini
description: Cialdini identifies a small set of psychological principles—reciprocity, commitment, social proof, authority, liking, and scarcity—that reliably drive compliance, based on both experiments and his own fieldwork inside sales organizations.

title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
subtitle: Dale Carnegie
description: A decades-old but still widely read guide to basic interpersonal communication—genuine interest in others, remembering names, and avoiding direct criticism—that remains a common reference point for practical people skills.

title: Nonviolent Communication: A Language of Life
subtitle: Marshall B. Rosenberg
description: A structured communication framework (observation, feeling, need, request) designed to express honestly and listen empathically even in conflict, developed by Rosenberg from his work in mediation and civil rights contexts.

title: Predictably Irrational
subtitle: Dan Ariely
description: Ariely's behavioral economics experiments show that people's departures from 'rational' decision-making are not random but follow consistent, predictable patterns—relevant to understanding real human judgment rather than idealized models of it.

title: The Righteous Mind
subtitle: Jonathan Haidt
description: Haidt examines why people with different political and moral commitments struggle to persuade each other, arguing moral judgments are grounded in intuition first and reasoning second.

title: Never Split the Difference
subtitle: Chris Voss (with Tahl Raz)
description: A former FBI lead hostage negotiator's account of negotiation tactics—tactical empathy, calibrated questions, active listening—developed under genuinely high-stakes conditions and adapted for everyday use.

title: Quiet: The Power of Introverts in a World That Can't Stop Talking
subtitle: Susan Cain
description: Cain reviews personality psychology research on introversion and extroversion, challenging the assumption that effective communication and leadership require an extroverted style.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
subtitle: Yuval Noah Harari
description: A sweeping account of human history organized around the idea that shared stories—money, nations, religions—are what allow large numbers of strangers to cooperate, a useful broad lens on group behavior.

title: Blink: The Power of Thinking Without Thinking
subtitle: Malcolm Gladwell
description: Gladwell explores rapid, unconscious judgment ('thin-slicing'), presenting cases where snap decisions outperform deliberation as well as cases where the same fast judgments go badly wrong.

title: Daniel Kahneman
subtitle: Psychologist; 2002 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Kahneman and his longtime collaborator Amos Tversky founded much of modern behavioral economics by documenting systematic biases in human judgment under uncertainty.

title: Robert Cialdini
subtitle: Professor emeritus, Arizona State University
description: Cialdini's persuasion research is unusual for its method: he took entry-level jobs in sales, fundraising, and advertising to study compliance professionals' techniques directly, work he later extended in 'Pre-Suasion.'

title: Jonathan Haidt
subtitle: Social psychologist, NYU Stern School of Business
description: Beyond his work on moral intuition, Haidt co-founded Heterodox Academy to promote viewpoint diversity in research, and more recently wrote 'The Anxious Generation' on adolescent mental health and technology.

title: Behavioral Economics
description: A field, recognized with the 2017 Nobel Memorial Prize awarded to Richard Thaler, that studies how real human decision-making systematically departs from the rational-actor assumptions of classical economic models.

title: Dual-Process Theory of Cognition
description: A well-studied framework in cognitive psychology distinguishing fast, automatic thought processes from slower, effortful, deliberate ones, used to explain a wide range of judgment and decision-making phenomena.
